name: Lead: came for stained glass, sheet for gutters and flats
summary: Soft, dense, low-melting grey metal that weathers to a protective carbonate patina. In Albion it holds the glass (the H-section cames of the Tristram band and the lancets) and keeps the water off the glass roofs (the valley gutters on the arcade lines and the porch's lead flat).

formation.how: Lead is smelted from galena and refined; for building it is cast, then milled (rolled) to sheet, or milled or extruded into came. It melts at 327 degC and is so soft it can be scratched with a fingernail, so it is worked cold: bossed and dressed to shape on a roof, opened and folded round glass at the bench. Freshly cut it is silvery with a bluish tint; in air it tarnishes to dull grey under a thin, protective film in which lead carbonate is common, with sulfate or chloride in city or sea air.

appearance.text: Freshly cut: 'shiny silvery with a bluish tint'; 'tarnishes to dull gray on exposure to air'.

patina.text: In moist air lead forms a protective layer; 'Lead(II) carbonate is a common constituent', with lead(II) sulfate or chloride in urban or maritime air; the layer makes the metal 'effectively inert under atmospheric conditions'.

thermalMovement.conditions: one metre of sheet over a 50 K swing between a winter night and a summer noon on a roof
thermalMovement.note: why sheet lead is laid in bays fixed at the head only

optics.note: Weathered lead shows only its patina: a dull, pale bluish grey, matt to satin. Fresh-cut lead (a scratch, a new cut edge of came) is briefly metallic; its complex index was not read here.

acoustic.note: Came and gutters are not absorbing surfaces. The drumming of rain on a lead flat is Sound's.

colour.note: the cames seen against the light, from inside

photograph: Old lead is a soft, pale bluish grey, dull, with white carbonate blooms where water lingers and dark streaks where it runs.
Sheet lead lies in bays with rolls and drips; its surface is gently undulating, never flat like metal sheet.
Came seen from inside against the sky is a black line with a narrow soft highlight on its rounded or flat leaf; soldered joints are small bright-grey lumps at each junction.
